youtube.baslik: Does a baby who startles at loud sounds hear normally? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In behavioral observation audiometry, or BOA, an example three-month-old startles clearly at loud sounds, yet frequency-specific ABR estimates thresholds near seventy decibels in both ears; despite responding to loud sounds, the baby has a moderately severe hearing loss. So BOA is reported as a minimal response level, not a threshold, and threshold estimation at this age relies on objective tests.
